html:
The Pequawket were a band of the Abenaki people who lived along the upper Saco River, around today's Fryeburg, Maine and Conway, New Hampshire, in the 1600s and 1700s. They farmed the river meadows and hunted in the White Mountains.

During Dummer's War with New England, a party of Massachusetts scalp hunters under John Lovewell attacked them in May 1725. In the battle, known as Lovewell's Fight or the Battle of Pequawket, the Pequawket leader Paugus was killed, as were Lovewell and many of his men. Afterwards most Pequawket moved north to the Abenaki mission at Odanak in New France.
